newsitem.title: USA: Pa. Gov signs electricity deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Pa. Gov signs electricity deregulation bill.

text.p: Pennsylvania Gov Tom Ridge Tuesday signed into law a bill to deregulate the state's electricity market, the governor's office said.
The bill allows Pennsylvania residents to choose their electric company by the year 2001.
Ridge said the measure will lower electric bills and introduce competition into the electric utility market for the first time in state history.

"Today, Pennsylvania becomes the fourth state in the nation to transform the utility industry from a monopoly to free market competition," Ridge said in a statement. The other states are California, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island.
New Jersey is expected to unveil the second phase of its study on electricity deregulation by the end of the year.
Pennsylvania's deregulation measure last month passed the state Senate by a vote of 40-10 and the House by a vote of 171-28.
Ridge said Pennsylvania has a reputation as a high-cost utility state and consumers pay on average 15 percent more than their neighbors.
Under the new law, a pilot program will begin in 1997. Starting in 1999, one-third of consumers would be phased in each year until full competition is reached in 2001.
